objectives: Consolidate accurate reading of taught m/s/t/a/p/n patterns.
Develop smoother repeated reading without sacrificing decoding accuracy.
Check decoding, spelling, comprehension, sequencing and fluency-related needs separately.
concepts: Fluency grows from accurate decoding through repeated supported reading.
Speed is not useful if accuracy or meaning is lost.
A consolidation checkpoint should identify the next specific instructional need.

definitions.definition: Accurate, increasingly smooth and appropriately paced reading.
Fast, reliable recognition of a well-practised pattern or word.
Reading the same controlled text more than once to improve accuracy and smoothness.

workedExamples: Decode nap accurately, then reread it smoothly.
Read the controlled sentence twice: first for accuracy, second for smoother phrasing and meaning.
If accuracy is high but pace is slow, use repeated accurate reading rather than guessing.
commonMistakes: Ignoring meaning while focusing on speed.
Treating slow but accurate reading as decoding failure.
keyTakeaways: Use evidence to identify the next need.
revisionPoints: Accurate decoding → repeated reading → smoother phrasing → meaning check.

higherOrderThinking: Choose an appropriate intervention for slow but accurate reading.
mixedReview: Decode, spell, read, sequence and comprehend.

mistakeBasedRevision: Guessing error → return to sound-by-sound decoding.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat the exact weak component before advancing.

activities.name: Three-read routine
steps: Read a third time while checking meaning.

outcomes: Learner reads taught n-containing CVC words accurately with at least 90% accuracy.
Learner improves smoothness across repeated controlled reading.
Learner maintains comprehension while rereading for fluency.
Learner's remaining needs can be classified as decoding, spelling, comprehension or fluency.

questions.question: Which reading shows accurate decoding of “nap”?
Which word has the same ending as “man”?
What should fluent reading become more like after accurate practice?
What should the learner do when a word is not automatic yet?
options: Decode it accurately and reread it

questions.question: Why is rereading useful for fluency?
options: It builds accurate and smoother word recognition
It removes the need to decode

questions.question: Which word is correctly spelled with final n?
Read: “Nan sat at a mat.” Where did Nan sit?
Read: “Nan had a map.” What did Nan have?
Which sequence is correct for the passage: “Nan sat at a mat. Nan sat. Nan had a map.”?
options: sat at a mat → sat → had a map
had a map → sat → sat at a mat
sat → had a map → sat at a mat

questions.question: Which behavior supports both fluency and comprehension?
options: Accurate rereading with attention to meaning

questions.question: If a learner is accurate but very slow, what should practice emphasize?
options: Repeated accurate reading for smoother phrasing

questions.question: What is the purpose of this checkpoint?
options: Measure accurate, increasingly smooth reading and identify remaining needs
